questions.q: Building on Descartes’ “I think, therefore, I am,” what does the editorial say?
options: “I see, therefore, I believe”
Not quite. The article says: “I am, therefore, God is” – a creature’s existence points to a Creator.
“I work, therefore, I am”
Not quite. The article says: “I am, therefore, God is” – a creature’s existence points to a Creator.
“I am, therefore, God is” – a creature’s existence points to a Creator
Yes. Simple logic applied to one’s own being.
“I doubt, therefore, nothing is certain”
Not quite. The article says: “I am, therefore, God is” – a creature’s existence points to a Creator.
questions.rationale: “By applying the same logic, one can say, ‘I am, therefore, God is.’”

questions.q: How does the editorial use subatomic particles to answer the question, “How can one believe in a God who is unseen?”
options: They show that everything can be seen with the right tools
Not quite. The article says: They show that something can exist without being visible.
They show that something can exist without being visible
Right. Being seen is not the test of being real.
They show that scientists are often wrong
Not quite. The article says: They show that something can exist without being visible.
They show that matter is an illusion
Not quite. The article says: They show that something can exist without being visible.
questions.rationale: “A subatomic particle, although not visible, does exist. This shows that for something to exist, it is not necessary that it should be visible.”

questions.q: What does it mean, in the article, to look at every affair “in its eternal context”?
options: To plan carefully for old age
Not quite. The article says: To value only what will count in the Hereafter, and treat as worthless what will be worthless there.
To ignore present duties
Not quite. The article says: To value only what will count in the Hereafter, and treat as worthless what will be worthless there.
To value only what will count in the Hereafter, and treat as worthless what will be worthless there
Well read. This is the outlook of faith.
To study the history of past nations
Not quite. The article says: To value only what will count in the Hereafter, and treat as worthless what will be worthless there.
questions.rationale: “We will consider everything which will become worthless in the next world as worthless now, no matter how great a worldly price it may seem to command.”

questions.q: The article calls this world “a preview of the Hereafter.” How should its pleasures be understood?
options: As temptations with no purpose
Not quite. The article says: As a drop that points to an ocean – meant to increase longing for the lasting joys to come.
As a drop that points to an ocean – meant to increase longing for the lasting joys to come
Yes. The loss is to mistake the sample for the whole.
As rewards already earned in full
Not quite. The article says: As a drop that points to an ocean – meant to increase longing for the lasting joys to come.
As all the happiness there is
Not quite. The article says: As a drop that points to an ocean – meant to increase longing for the lasting joys to come.
questions.rationale: “So that he may see one drop of water, and realize that it is indicative of a vast ocean beyond.”

questions.q: “No steam or gas ever drives anything until it is confined.” What does the article apply this to?
options: People work best under pressure from others
Not quite. The article says: A life grows only when it is focused, dedicated and disciplined.
Freedom is harmful to the young
Not quite. The article says: A life grows only when it is focused, dedicated and disciplined.
Engines need regular repair
Not quite. The article says: A life grows only when it is focused, dedicated and disciplined.
A life grows only when it is focused, dedicated and disciplined
Correct. There is a price for every end.
questions.rationale: “No life ever grows until it is focused, dedicated, and disciplined.”

questions.q: When drought cut the Ivory Coast’s electricity, a businessman said he had never realised how hot it was. What does the article take from this?
options: Hot countries need more power stations
Not quite. The article says: People live in an artificial sense of ownership and freedom; death will show how things really stand.
Comfort makes people healthier
Not quite. The article says: People live in an artificial sense of ownership and freedom; death will show how things really stand.
Businessmen should work from home
Not quite. The article says: People live in an artificial sense of ownership and freedom; death will show how things really stand.
People live in an artificial sense of ownership and freedom; death will show how things really stand
Well reasoned. Freedom was a test, not a right.
questions.rationale: “When death comes, it will dawn on an individual, all of a sudden, that he had just been fooling himself: he had been given freedom as a test whereas he had thought it was his right.”

questions.q: “Madam, you are in Russia now, not America.” What wider point does the article make with this remark?
options: Every country is the same at heart
Not quite. The article says: Man lives in a world made by God, not by himself, and must live by God’s scheme for it.
Man lives in a world made by God, not by himself, and must live by God’s scheme for it
Right. The prophets came to make that scheme known.
One should never leave one’s homeland
Not quite. The article says: Man lives in a world made by God, not by himself, and must live by God’s scheme for it.
Travellers should keep their opinions to themselves
Not quite. The article says: Man lives in a world made by God, not by himself, and must live by God’s scheme for it.
questions.rationale: “Man, then, is not in his own country: he is living in the country of God.”

questions.q: Why, according to the article, is the mind at its freshest in the morning?
options: Because the air is cooler
Not quite. The article says: During sleep it sorts and files the day’s impressions, leaving it clear – and there are few distractions.
During sleep it sorts and files the day’s impressions, leaving it clear – and there are few distractions
Yes. The best hours for reading, reflection and planning.
Because the day’s news has not yet arrived
Not quite. The article says: During sleep it sorts and files the day’s impressions, leaving it clear – and there are few distractions.
Because breakfast gives energy
Not quite. The article says: During sleep it sorts and files the day’s impressions, leaving it clear – and there are few distractions.
questions.rationale: “During sleep, the mind sorts out the observations and thoughts and stores them in their respective files… his mind has been cleared of all thoughts and is blank once again.”

questions.q: What habit does the article call “one-sided reporting”?
options: Speaking for too long
Not quite. The article says: Telling only what the other person did, while leaving out one’s own part in the matter.
Telling only what the other person did, while leaving out one’s own part in the matter
Well read. It is unfair and solves nothing.
Repeating what others have said
Not quite. The article says: Telling only what the other person did, while leaving out one’s own part in the matter.
Reading only one newspaper
Not quite. The article says: Telling only what the other person did, while leaving out one’s own part in the matter.
questions.rationale: “Every person has the habit of recounting an incident in such a manner that only the involvement of the other person is apparent, whilst remaining silent about their own involvement.”

questions.article: All That Glitters Is Not Gold
questions.q: A necklace bought as gold proved to be brass on the goldsmith’s touchstone. What does the story warn of?
options: The poor are often dishonest
Not quite. The article says: Deeds we think of as gold will be tested on God’s touchstone, and only the genuine will have value.
Gold should be bought only from shops
Not quite. The article says: Deeds we think of as gold will be tested on God’s touchstone, and only the genuine will have value.
Deeds we think of as gold will be tested on God’s touchstone, and only the genuine will have value
Exactly. Self-satisfaction is no proof.
One should never help strangers
Not quite. The article says: Deeds we think of as gold will be tested on God’s touchstone, and only the genuine will have value.
questions.rationale: “In the next world, God will judge everybody’s actions on His own touchstone. The value of gold will only be attached to those actions which are proved to be made of gold.”
